# ghp-dashboard-demo

A demo dashboard for a prostate cancer cohort, built with Vite, Vue 3, TypeScript, and Chart.js (run with Bun). It is published to GitHub Pages.

**All data in this repository is synthetic.** It is generated by `scripts/generate-sample-data.ts` from assumed distributions and does not come from any patient.

## What it shows

- Five sub-cohort tabs. The first, **Newly diagnosed (localized)**, has full content. The other four are placeholders waiting for data.
- KPI tiles and nine chart types: doughnut, pie, bar, stacked bar, horizontal bar, scatter, line (time series and Kaplan-Meier survival), and radar.
- A "Data last updated" timestamp taken from `meta.generated_at` in the JSON file, plus the time the site was last deployed.
- A "Preview a JSON file" button that renders a local JSON file in the browser without uploading it anywhere.

## Data format

The dashboard reads one file, `public/data/cohort.json`. Its structure is defined in `src/types/cohort.ts`:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "meta": { "title": "...", "cohort": "...", "data_source": "...", "generated_at": "2026-10-23T12:00:00Z" },
  "subcohorts": [
    {
      "id": "newly-diagnosed",
      "name": "Newly diagnosed (localized)",
      "status": "ready",
      "description": "...",
      "kpis": [{ "label": "Patients", "value": "300" }],
      "charts": [
        {
          "id": "race-distribution",
          "title": "Race and ethnicity",
          "type": "doughnut",
          "labels": ["White", "Black"],
          "datasets": [{ "label": "Patients", "data": [186, 63] }]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `chart.type` is one of `pie`, `doughnut`, `bar`, `horizontalBar`, `stackedBar`, `line`, `scatter`, `radar`.
- Scatter datasets use `{ "x": number, "y": number }` points. All other types use plain numbers with `labels`.
- A sub-cohort with `"status": "placeholder"` and no charts is shown as a placeholder tab.
- `meta.generated_at` must be an ISO 8601 timestamp. The app refuses files with a different `schema_version`.

## Local development

```bash
bun install
bun run scripts/generate-sample-data.ts   # optional: regenerate the synthetic data
bun run dev
```

Build for production with `bun run build`. The output goes to `dist/`.

## Publishing an update

1. Replace `public/data/cohort.json` with the new file. Either commit the file, or use GitHub's **Add file > Upload files** in the web UI.
2. Push to `main`. The workflow in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds the site and deploys it to GitHub Pages.
3. The header shows the new `generated_at` value once the deployment finishes.

To check a file before publishing, use **Preview a JSON file** on the site, or run `bun run dev` and use the same button.

## GitHub Pages setup

In the repository settings, set **Pages > Build and deployment > Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
